Preview

Private, from start to finish.

Use Encrypt for ordinary files and Decrypt for .efs containers. Imports are routed to the right tab automatically.

Use the Extract ZIP action on an imported or decrypted .zip file. The extracted files appear in the same list under the archive name. Password-protected ZIP files are unsupported.

Encryption protects original names, file types, folder details, and contents. Downloads get random UUID names that you can change before saving. Once a download is requested, the encrypted output leaves the export list. A retry copy stays in this tab for two minutes. Check your browser downloads to confirm it saved.

In Decrypt, unlock filenames with a password to reveal matching names in the upper list. Select the files you want to decrypt; the results appear in the lower list with an inline preview. Folder contents can be selected individually. Use Preview beside an unlocked MOV, MP4, or WebM to play it on demand. The app decrypts the bytes the player requests without creating a full decrypted file.

There is no password recovery. To change a password, select decrypted files and choose Re-encrypt selected. Only the selected files move to Encrypt. You must delete old encrypted copies yourself.

There is no fixed app file-size limit. Encrypted output uses temporary browser storage when supported. If the browser cannot store it, a supported browser can offer a retry to a folder you choose. The folder receives only encrypted .efs files. Decryption keeps results in this tab as browser-managed Blobs. Large files can reach browser limits. Temporary encrypted files can remain after a crash; the app removes them on a later visit. Progress shows the percentage of content bytes processed. Password checks and final disk writes take additional time. PDF previews use a locally bundled renderer. Google Drive, Dropbox, and OneDrive connect only when requested and download selected files directly into this browser. Tokens and temporary download links stay in memory. Provider scripts load only when you use their importer.

This is an initial implementation awaiting independent security review. Your browser and the code delivered to it are part of the trust boundary.
